newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/2 point near finish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/2 point near finish.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices added to early gains to finish the shortened session about 1/2 point higher Friday, traders said.
Munis joined a Treasury rally after the January producer price index showed a 0.3 percent drop instead of the 0.3 percent increase economists had forecast.
The government long bond was up 9/32 at 101 to yield 6.55 percent, and muni traders said their market was following along.
"We're up at least 1/2 point on the offered side," one trader said, though he said not many bonds are changing hands and activity has basically ended until after Monday's Presidents' Day holiday.
Next week's new issue calendar totals $1.97 billion, lower than this week's $3 billion total, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.5 billion, topped off by a $246 million Hempstead Industrial Development Authority, N.Y., deal through Smith Barney Inc.
Competitive sales total $476 million in 53 deals, with a $65.5 million Arlington Independent School District, Texas, deal on Thursday the largest issue.
In futures, the March municipal contract was up 20/32 to 117-26/32, while March T-bonds rose 19/32 to 113-30/32. The MOB spread was 124 ticks, widening one from 123 at the close Thursday.
In the secondary market, actively traded issues included Dade County, Fla., FGIC water and sewer system 5-1/4s of 2026, bid at 5.54 percent net, down four basis points.
Sikeston, Mo., MBIA electric 5.0s of 2022, were bid at 5.53 percent net, down five basis points.
